scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The imported intervals are Basutoland1878–1914, Lesotho1914–1938 and Lesotho1960–present. All include colonial coverage, so the shared narrative is a regional history rather than a claim that all three were independent states. CanonicalcardLesotho contains periods from1878 tosupport the earliest alias. No imported polygons, historical-basemap data or modern dataset are edited.

Government historical text was read in indexed full paragraphs; direct page access failed. Its1822/1824 simplification and generic ethnic prehistory are not used.1868Britishannexation,1871Capeadministration and1884directCrownrule are distinct events; the page discusses the last two for its map period. The1966independence date is cross-checked in the African Peer Review report.

The2010APRMreport was accessed as a401-page searchable PDF, but only relevant historical passages on printed pages33–34 and associated executive-summary entries were read.1970authoritarian rule,1986military takeover and1993multiparty restoration are kept distinct. Its2010present-tense stability assessments are not projected into2026. An apparent1990/1991inconsistency about a later military leadership change is outside the claims and not repeated.

Thaba Bosiu is sourced to Lesotho’s ministry submission to the UNESCO Tentative List inDecember2025. That is not World Heritage inscription or independent UNESCO endorsement of every historical or geological assertion. Oral tradition about night-time height is labelled as tradition. The submission’s geological description and claim of purely non-violent state formation are not adopted.

Sekokotoana’s2020essay was read in full. The two stories use her explanation of home decoration and her own ceramic plate, including remembered parental advice. Images credited to other artists are not silently assigned to her or automatically located in Lesotho. Her view of declining practice is attributed rather than treated as proof of extinction.

British Museum record2012,2018.4 was read in full indexed text; direct fetching failed. It records a blanket purchased from the manufacturer in2012, made inRandfonteinSouthAfrica, rather than an excavated Lesotho object. The curator qualifies the traditional origin story and the alleged manufacturing error behind stripes, so neither is asserted as fact. Current production rates, prices and universal dress customs are not inferred.

The Iziko exhibition was read for Makoanyane’s biography, objects and1935musiciancommission. Mother/child and sleeping-mat sculptures are dated only within the artist’s1909–1944lifetime. Commissioned art can illuminate subjects and skilled representation without being a photographic census. Some biography depends on dealerCGDamant’s1951account; speculative illness, alleged beliefs and an unexplained unmade eighth figure are not simplified into certainties. No2022museumopening claim is inferred from a future-tense announcement.

Nyabela’sDecember2022Morija report was downloaded as a31-pagePDF. Selected sections including printed pages11–16 and19–21 were read, not every historical chapter. The public words across three music stories share one budget. First attestation is not invention; disputed ethnic origins and absolute gender restrictions are not adopted.2007/2008revival evidence comes from named local settings. Lesiba sound is attributed to breath and quill; lekope to a plucked string and mouth resonator. Healing-dance evidence concerns documented belief and performance, not clinical efficacy.

Morija’s archive and projects pages were read directly. Specific printed holdings andTheHub2015opening are supported; no unread newspaper article or quantitative educational impact is invented. The two public descriptions use a combined budget below200words as a conservative treatment of related museum pages.

EAP845’sproject description and outcomes were read directly. Actual digitisation outcomes are not confused with the initial12,000-page ambition. The card uses source types and collection dates, not unsupported claims about a particular marriage custom from unread interviews. Missionary selection and mediation are explained.

The ICOMOS2013Sehlabathebe assessment was read in indexed text for printed page27; direct PDF fetching failed. The2013WorldHeritageCommittee decision was read directly and confirms extension. The evaluation’s pigment/motif descriptions concern Sehlabathebe. Image totals for the much larger SouthAfricancomponent are not assigned toLesotho, and uncertain paintings are not dated to a single creation year. Assessment and inscription decision are distinct documents, kept within a combined200-word public budget.

New text is author-checked pending independent historical-depth review. Structural checks do not certify exhaustive history, current constitutional details or border precision. No undocumented toilet, food or family practice is invented to fill a category.

proposedOverrides.summary: Lesotho became independent from Britain on 4 October 1966. Its earlier colonial name was Basutoland. The separate map records cover parts of a continuing regional history, rather than three unrelated countries.

sharedAssociations.basis: The imported name and geometry identify colonial Basutoland and the territory later independent as Lesotho. The shared regional history separates map intervals from political status and1966 independence.
